thread:
ryan: heads up — CI is flapping on quant-eval jobs, lots of runner tasks stuck in SCHED_WAIT since yesterday night :grimacing:
anna: saw that. Which job? job/quant-eval-2026-03-18-11 is timing out repeatedly, p95 latency skyrockets before hang
sara: stacktrace from the runner attached in the job logs shows threads blocked on scheduler::acquire_pool_lock
kevin: repro locally with --stress-scheduler and you can see the same stack:
kevin: ```
THREAD 12 WAITING at scheduler.cpp:142 acquire_pool_lock
  at pthread_cond_wait+0x7
  at scheduler::wait_for_slot scheduler.cpp:88
```
ryan: thanks. any recent changes touching the runner scheduler?
anna: yes — PR #1289 (kevin) changed the eviction ordering to prefer KV cache retention; touched scheduler acquire/release paths
sara: regression window matches. can we bisect to confirm?
kevin: running a bisect now across the last 10 commits on main for the runner image. keeping you posted (this is on dedicated-quant image tag: rwinf/runner:canary-20260317)
ci-bot: job/quant-eval-2026-03-18-11 retriggered by @kevin
kevin: quick note — when I force the runner to drop to single-scheduler-thread mode the hang goes away. points to a contention bug in the multi-thread path
ryan: if that's true we should hold the canary and block the dedicated rollout. @product-owners — FYI
anna: agree. put a hold on the rollout and pin traffic to previous image rn: rwinf/runner:stable-20260310
sara: can we craft a minimal patch? maybe add timeout on acquire and log owner stack. quick mitigation first
kevin: I pushed a hotfix branch that adds a backoff + watchdog and improved logs: kevin/scheduler-backoff-20260318. still running integration smoke locally
ryan: good. let's run the quant eval suite against the hotfix image before unblocking. kevin — can you deploy image to canary-2 and run the same job id?
kevin: deployed rwinf/runner:canary-backfix-20260318 to canary-2. starting job/quant-eval-2026-03-18-12 now
ci-bot: job/quant-eval-2026-03-18-12 started on canary-2
sara: initial metrics look promising — latency stable, no SCHED_WAIT spikes in first 20m
ryan: if canary passes full suite, plan is: 1) promote hotfix to canary-primary, 2) run full quant regression, 3) unhold rollout. otherwise rollback to stable and open a formal P0
anna: adding a note to the release tracker and tagging eng-oncall
kevin: full suite finished: all tests green; no hangs. uploading logs and diff vs stable to the eval dashboard
sara: thanks. I'll run an overnight job to be extra sure. also adding a gating check in CI to detect >3 threads stuck >30s on acquire_pool_lock
ryan: nice. once overnight looks good, we'll merge the hotfix and cut a patched runner image. good triage all
dev-bot: deploy note created: deploy/runner/canary-backfix-20260318 -> canary-primary (pending approval) :rocket:
kevin: filing postmortem draft with timeline and root cause (contention introduced by eviction ordering + missing backoff). will attach mitigations and follow-ups
anna: closing loop: release hold removed after final smoke pass. keeping the rollback plan ready for 24h
ryan: thanks team. follow-ups: add scheduler unit tests for contention, add CI gate to fail early on this pattern, longer-term rework of eviction/scheduler interaction
ci-bot: job/quant-eval-2026-03-18-12 completed successfully (duration 48m)
